newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia airline to fly more international routes.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia airline to fly more international routes.

text.p: Merpati Nusantara Airlines, a subsidiary of Indonesia's national carrier Garuda, has said it will fly more international routes, the Jakarta Post reported on Saturday.
Merpati's director of operations, Prasetyo Wisaksono, was quoted as saying that the airline plans to link Jakarta and Hong Kong via Medan in North Sumatra later this year.
Merpati had already received approval from the Indonesian government and the Hong Kong authorities, Prasetyo said.
A Jakarta to Melbourne route, flying three times a week, was also planned for later this month, the official Antara news agency said on Saturday.

Last year the company lost 93.12 billion rupiah ($39.71 million). This year it plans to reduce losses to 63.74 billion rupiah ($27.18 million) by terminating less profitable routes such as the one from Ambon in the Maluku Islands to Darwin which ceased operations last month.
